native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: En este panel agregado 1975-2015 con sólo dos grupos (SSA y LMC), un aumento del gasto en educación (Adjusted savings: education expenditure, % del GNI) NO se traduce en una respuesta mayor del ingreso per cápita en el África Subsahariana que en los países de Ingreso Medio-Bajo. La única especificación propiamente de-tendenciada que los datos permiten — la elasticidad log-log en primeras diferencias para LMC, 1976-2015, con Newey-West HAC SE — es pequeña y positiva (β ≈ +0.07, R² ≈ 0.05); para SSA es inestimable (T=5, GNIpc sólo 2010-2015). En niveles —donde los residuos muestran fuerte autocorrelación (Ljung-Box p≈0)— ambas series presentan asociación negativa (GNIpc sube monótonamente mientras la participación educativa se estanca o cae), pero la interacción agrupada D_SSA × log(EducExp) sobre la única ventana común (2010-2015, T=11) es positiva (+1.3, HAC-SE 0.04), de modo que la elasticidad de niveles de SSA (≈ −0.42) es menos negativa que la de LMC (≈ −1.73). Lectura sintetizada: dirección — igual o ligeramente menor en SSA (no mayor); magnitud cualitativa — muy pequeña, ≈ 0.05 de elasticidad una vez descontada la tendencia. Caveats: N=2 ⇒ inferencia entre grupos esencialmente descriptiva; SSA GNIpc truncada a 5 obs; educación medida como % GNI no como nivel absoluto; Y es GNI pc no estrictamente PIB pc; sin IV factible.
native_result.WorkflowB: (a) Inspección: wide CSV 12×45, 2 grupos × 6 indicadores × 41 años; 84/492 celdas faltantes (17.1 %); SSA GNIpc sólo 5 obs (2010-2015). (b) Re-shaping a panel largo (82×9) y trayectorias descriptivas por periodo clave. (c) Correlaciones log(EducExp) vs log(GNIpc) por grupo y por ventana común + correlaciones en primeras diferencias. (d) Regresiones por grupo: log(GNIpc) ~ log(EducExp) + (log(PrimEnr), log(SecEnr), ΔExports) en niveles con Newey-West HAC; submuestras 1975-2015 y 1975-2007 (pre-GFC). (e) Panel agrupado 2010-2015 (T=11) con interacción D_SSA × log(EducExp), controles y tendencia temporal; variante sin tendencia. (f) Robustness en primeras diferencias para LMC (1976-2015); SSA FD documentada como inestimable (T=4). (g) Síntesis: signo, magnitud y dirección relativa entre los dos grupos; redacción de la hipótesis en lenguaje natural.

sub_hypo.text: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it.
sub_hypo.context: Developing countries outside Sub-Saharan Africa compared with developing countries within Sub-Saharan Africa.
sub_hypo.relations: Increasing education expenditure has a more pronounced effect on per capita GDP in developing countries outside Sub-Saharan Africa than in those within Sub-Saharan Africa.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it

sub_hypo.text: An increase in education expenditure as a percentage of GNI does not translate into a greater per capita income response in Sub-Saharan Africa than in lower-middle-income countries; the synthesized response is equal or slightly smaller in SSA.
sub_hypo.context: Aggregate panel of two groups, SSA and LMC, during 1975–2015. Between-group inference is essentially descriptive because N=2, SSA GNI per capita has only five observations within 2010–2015, and no feasible instrumental-variable analysis is available.
variables: Adjusted savings: education expenditure (% of GNI)
sub_hypo.relations: The hypothesized income response to education expenditure is not greater in SSA than in LMC. The synthesized trend-adjusted elasticity is qualitatively very small, approximately 0.05. Education expenditure measures a share of GNI rather than an absolute spending level, and income is GNI per capita rather than GDP per capita.

sub_hypo.text: For LMC, the first-difference log-log relationship between education expenditure and GNI per capita is small and positive; the corresponding SSA relationship cannot be estimated.
sub_hypo.context: LMC, 1976–2015, using first differences and Newey-West HAC standard errors. SSA has only five GNI per capita observations within 2010–2015; the workflow records four first-difference observations and treats the specification as inestimable.
variables: Adjusted savings: education expenditure (% of GNI)
sub_hypo.relations: For LMC, Δlog(GNI per capita) is positively associated with Δlog(education expenditure), with elasticity approximately +0.07 and R² approximately 0.05. No corresponding trend-adjusted SSA elasticity is estimable.

sub_hypo.text: In levels, education expenditure and GNI per capita are negatively associated in both SSA and LMC, while regression residuals exhibit strong autocorrelation.
sub_hypo.context: Group-specific log-level analyses in the 1975–2015 panel, with a 1975–2007 pre-global-financial-crisis subsample and a common-window comparison; SSA income coverage is restricted to five observations within 2010–2015. Regressions use Newey-West HAC standard errors and specifications with enrollment and export controls.
variables: Adjusted savings: education expenditure (% of GNI)
Exports of goods and services (annual % growth)
sub_hypo.relations: Negative association between log(education expenditure) and log(GNI per capita) in both groups: GNI per capita rises monotonically while the education expenditure share stagnates or declines. Residual autocorrelation is strong, with Ljung-Box p approximately zero; these level associations are not the trend-adjusted response.

sub_hypo.text: In the common-window pooled levels model, SSA has a less negative education-expenditure elasticity of GNI per capita than LMC.
sub_hypo.context: Common window 2010–2015, with 11 pooled observations. The workflow fits an SSA interaction, enrollment and export controls, and a time trend, plus a variant without the trend; inference uses HAC standard errors.
variables: Adjusted savings: education expenditure (% of GNI)
Exports of goods and services (annual % growth)
sub_hypo.relations: The D_SSA × log(education expenditure) interaction is positive, approximately +1.3 with HAC standard error 0.04. The implied levels elasticity is approximately −0.42 for SSA versus −1.73 for LMC, making SSA's association less negative rather than establishing a larger positive trend-adjusted response.
